title: Service Bus Topics and Subscriptions
description: Use topics and subscriptions to broadcast messages to multiple independent consumers.

data.text: A Service Bus topic works like a newspaper subscription. The publisher sends one copy of each message to the topic. Every subscription registered on the topic receives its own copy of each message, filtered and stored independently.

data.title: Create a Topic and Subscriptions (Azure CLI)
data.content: Create a topic and two subscriptions with filters:
data.code:
az servicebus topic create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --namespace-name myNamespace \
  --name orders

az servicebus topic subscription create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --namespace-name myNamespace \
  --topic-name orders \
  --name high-value-orders \
  --filter-sql-expression "orderTotal > 1000"

az servicebus topic subscription create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --namespace-name myNamespace \
  --topic-name orders \
  --name all-orders

data.title: Filter Rules
items: TrueFilter: All messages pass through (default for new subscriptions).
SQLFilter: Use SQL-like expressions on message properties.
CorrelationFilter: Match messages by correlation ID or custom properties.
You can add or remove rules from any subscription at any time.

data.title: Send a Message to a Topic (JavaScript)
data.content: Sending to a topic uses the same sender as a queue; only the target path changes:

data.caption: Topic with multiple subscriptions and filters
data.definition:
graph TD
    P[Publisher] --> T[Topic: orders]
    T --> S1[Subscription: high-value-orders
    filter: total > 1000]
    T --> S2[Subscription: all-orders
    filter: TrueFilter]
    S1 --> R1[Receiver: VIP Team]
    S2 --> R2[Receiver: Fulfillment]
    S2 --> R3[Receiver: Analytics]

data.title: When to Use Topics
data.text: Use topics when multiple independent systems need the same event but should not be coupled together. For example, when an order is created, the shipping, billing, and notification systems can all react without knowing about each other.

data.title: Design a Subscription Strategy
data.description: An online store uses a user-events topic. Design three subscriptions for different teams.
steps: Create a subscription for the email team that only receives signup events.
Create a subscription for the analytics team that receives all user events.
Create a subscription for the fraud team that receives high-value purchase events.
data.expectedOutcome: Three subscriptions with appropriate SQL filters on an eventType property.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Topics broadcast one message copy to each subscription.
Subscriptions can filter messages with SQL-like rules.
Sending to a topic is the same API as sending to a queue; only the path changes.
Topics scale better than queues when many consumers need the same data.
data.takeaway: Next, you will learn how to handle failed messages with dead-lettering and retries.
